name: Swan Point
notes: microblades, hearths, and mammoth ivory working; no human remains

name: Xaasaa Na' (Upward Sun River)
notes: site of the oldest human remains discovered on the American side of Beringia

name: Cooper's Ferry
notes: controversial dating; if earlier dating is true it may support theory of early Americans arrival via a coastal route

name: Paisley Caves
notes: human DNA was recovered from the coprolites, and Western Stemmed points were found with them

name: Arlington Springs
notes: demonstrates that the earliest Paleoindians had watercraft capable of crossing channels, and lends credence to a coastal migration theory

name: Buttermilk Creek
notes: possible evidence of human settlement in the Americas that predates the Clovis culture

name: Meadowcroft Rockshelter
notes: long, deeply stratified sequence but oldest dates are controversial

name: Topper
notes: noted as a location of artifacts which may be earlier than the Clovis culture (disputed)

name: White Sands
notes: human footprints sit beside tracks of mammoths and ground sloths on an old lake shore

name: Blackwater Draw
notes: Clovis type site; Clovis points were found directly with Pleistocene animal bones

name: Anzick Site
notes: a child’s burial with Clovis artifacts

name: Lindenmeier Site
notes: the largest known Paleo-Indian Folsom site

name: Hoyo Negro
notes: a well-preserved skeleton found in a flooded cave

name: Naharon (Tulun)
notes: female skeleton; one of the oldest documented human finds in the Americas

name: Monte Verde
notes: wet-site settlement with wooden hut foundations, mastodon remains

name: Pedra Furada
notes: hundreds of rock paintings; charcoal from very ancient fires and stone shards (disputed)

name: Taima-Taima
notes: site of bi-pointed El Jobo points

name: Lapa Vermelha
notes: site of Luzia, skeletal remains of a Paleo-Indian woman

name: Fort Rock Cave
notes: site featured numerous well-preserved sagebrush sandals

name: Marmes Rockshelter
notes: human remains at the site were able to be dated with environmental, geological, and archaeological methods

name: Cueva de las Manos
notes: exceptional assemblage of cave art (stencilled outlines of human hands, but also many depictions of animals and hunting scenes)

name: Caverna da Pedra Pintada
notes: an Amazonian cave with early rock art and occupatio

name: Serranía de la Lindosa
notes: tens of thousands of red-ochre images, possibly including mastodons, giant sloths and Ice Age horses
